skill.name: offer-claims-registry
skill.description: Maintains traceable marketing claim and offer records with exact wording, evidence, disclosures, terms, review dates, and append-only history.
skill.summary: Register and trace approved marketing claims, evidence, and offer terms.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Two command-execution findings are confirmed: dynamic repository discovery and a registry write command. The remaining detections are safe Markdown, metadata, or fixed documentation links, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The repository root is resolved through shell command substitution before selecting the registry script.
remediation.suggestion: Use a host-provided, validated root and an allowlisted absolute script path without shell evaluation.

remediation.issue: The workflow invokes a local registry script that can append persistent claim events.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, validate the proposal path and schema, and execute a fixed argument array instead of a shell string.

content.value_statement: Marketing teams often lose approved wording, evidence, disclosures, and expiry dates across channels. This skill maintains traceable records through an append-only event workflow.
actual_capabilities: Registers proposed marketing claims with exact wording, scope, evidence references, disclosures, and review dates.
Tracks offer terms, eligibility, destinations, start dates, expiry dates, and status.
Queries the accepted claim or offer projection by aggregate identifier.
Reviews pending proposal events in order while preserving accepted and rejected history.
Records event identifiers, revisions, evidence gaps, and usage references for handoffs.
Regenerates human-readable claim and offer views from accepted projection state.
limitations: It does not determine legal compliance or replace a claim auditor.
It cannot invent evidence, substantiation, performance claims, or approved wording.
Canonical acceptance and mutation require a host capability with explicit write permission.
Execution depends on repository scripts and protocol files outside this skill folder.

use_cases.title: Register a substantiated claim
use_cases.description: Capture exact wording, evidence scope, disclosure, and review timing before channel teams reuse the claim.

use_cases.title: Maintain active offer terms
use_cases.description: Record pricing, eligibility, destination, start date, expiry date, and linked claims for a promotion.

use_cases.title: Review evidence gaps
use_cases.description: Inspect pending proposals, preserve unsupported wording as unresolved, and document acceptance or rejection reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Register one claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Register claim clm-014 with this exact wording: [wording]. Record evidence [source], disclosure [text], scope [scope], and review date [date].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner registration of a single supported claim

prompt_templates.title: Record an offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a proposal for offer [identifier]. Record price, discount, eligibility, code, destination, start date, end date, and linked claim identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Review pending proposals
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pending claim proposals in offset order. Identify evidence gaps, scope mismatches, required disclosures, and recommended accept or reject decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of unresolved registry events

prompt_templates.title: Audit claim usage across channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare accepted claim [identifier] with these rendered uses: [locations]. Report wording, scope, disclosure, evidence, revision, and expiry mismatches.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cross-channel provenance and consistency review

output_examples.input: Show the current status of claim clm-014.
output: Accepted wording: Reduces average setup time by 20 percent.
Scope: new customers using product version 4

output_examples.input: Review the proposal claiming customers save 50 percent.
output: Reason: the cited study supports 30 percent for enterprise customers only.
Next action: narrow the wording or provide broader evidence.
Terms: 15 percent off annual plans for new customers
Destination: accepted summer campaign landing page

best_practices: Use exact claim wording and record the measurable interpretation with its denominator.
Keep evidence scope, dates, disclosures, and review timing attached to every accepted claim.
Require explicit permission and preserve append-only history for every canonical change.
anti_patterns: Do not convert a missing-source marker into approved wording without independent evidence.
Do not edit the event stream or generated human views manually.
Do not expose host capability values in requests, files, or logs.

faq.question: Does this skill approve legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. It records claim and offer state, while an appropriate auditor evaluates a specific use.

faq.question: Can it create evidence for a claim?
faq.answer: No. Missing proof remains unresolved until a valid source with scope and date is provided.

faq.question: What can a standalone installation do?
faq.answer: It can prepare proposals, but it cannot append canonical events or claim approval without the required host capability.

faq.question: How are claim changes preserved?
faq.answer: Changes create append-only events with identifiers, revisions, and timestamps. Original approval events are not rewritten.

faq.question: How are expired offers handled?
faq.answer: Expiry creates a dated state change or tombstone. The original offer event remains in history.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code hosts that support the required workflow.
